Indian Standard 

SPECIFICATION FOR 
PRISMATIC ANGLE GAUGES 



( Reaffirmed 1998) 



1. Scope — Lays down requirements for prismatic angle gauges. 

1.1 These angle gauges together with the square block may be used to obtain any angle between and 
360 degrees in steps of 6 seconds. 

2. Material — The material of the gauges shall be suitable gauge steel which hss the properties of 
ageing stability in dimensions and wear resistance. Suitable examples of steels from IS: 1570-1961 
* Schedules for wrought steels for general engineering purposes ', are given below:

The working surfaces shall be hardened to not less than 800 HV.

3.3 The recommended sets of angle gauges are as under and shall be designated as Set A: 



t 



One each of 1, 3, 9/27 and 41 degrees 
Set A <{ One each of 1, 3, 9 and 27 minutes 
One each of 6, 18 and 30 seconds 



3,4 An alternative set of angle gauges ( designated as Set B ) is given below: 



{ 



One each of 1 , 3, 5, 1 5, 30 and 45 degrees 
Set B ^ One each of 1, 3, 5, 20 and 30 minutes 
One each of 6, 1 2 and 30 seconds 



Note — The above sets along with the square block enable any angle to be built up to 6 seconds, that is to within 
±3 seconds of the required angle. 

4. Tolerances — These shall be as given below: 



a 



SI Quality Limiting Value or Maximum 

Afo. Permissible Error 

i) The actual angle of each gauge including each ±2 seconds of arc 

interior angle of the precision square block shall 
agree with its nominal size 

ii) The measuring faces shall be flat 0*25 urn 

iii) The measuring faces shall be parallel transversely 1*0 t*m 

( that is, each point on a line drawn across a 
measuring face will be at the same vertical level ) 

iv) The side faces shall be ground flat 2*5 y.m 

v) The measuring faces shall be square to the side ±30 seconds or 2*5 (xm over the width 

faces 1 5 mm of measuring face 

vi) The surface roughness of the measuring feces shall 0*1 ^m Ra value, in accordance with 

be IS: 3073-1967 ' Assessment of surface 

roughness ' 

5. General Requirements 

5.1 The angle gauges shall be suitably stabilized by any one of the established stabilizing processes* 

5.2 The measuring faces shall be lapped flat to give a good wringing contact. The side faces shall be 
finely ground or lapped. The surface roughness of the gauging faces shall conform to the requirements 
given in 4. The gauging faces shall be free from corrosion marks, burrs or such other defects as would 
inhibit the satisfactory functioning of the surfaces. The edges shall be chamfered. 

5.3 A precision square block having its four sides lapped for wringing is provided for use with the angle 

gauges. 

5.4 A certificate giving the deviations of the angles of individual gauges from their nominal angle shall 
be issued with each set. 

6. Designation 

6.1 A set of prismatic angle gauges shall be designated by the name, the set to which it belongs and 
the number of this standard. 

Example: 

Prismatic Angle Gauge Set A, IS : 6231 

6.2 The individual angle gauges shall be designated by the nominal included angle and the number of 
this standard. 

Example: 

Prismatic Angle Gauge 3 Degrees, IS : 6231 

7. Marking — The gauges shall be marked with the following as shown in Fig. 2: , 

a) Nominal included angle; 

b) Symbol for the angle ( that is, /£\; and 

c) Manufacturer's name or trade-mark. 

2 



IS: 6231 -1971 

7.1 ISf Certification Marking — Details available with the Indian Standards Institution. 
9. Preservation and Packing 

8.1 All gauges shall be protected against climatic conditions by being covered with a hard drying 
lanolin, or other suitable non-corrosive preparation and shall be securely wrapped in waxed paper. 

8.2 Sets of gauges shall be packed in special boxes provided for the purpose, each set consisting of 1 3 
or 1 5 gauges as the case may be. 

EXPLANATORY NOTE 

Prismatic angle gauges can be used either individually or be wrung together to form composite 
angles. Appendix A gives examples for building angles, using angle gauges alone and angle gauges 
along with precision square block* j1 

APPENDIX A 

EXAMPLES OF BUILDING ANGLES 
A-1. Examples of Building Angles Usinj Angle Gauges 

Example 1: 

To build an angle : 24° 10' 18" 

a) Using Set A ( see Fig. 3 ) 

Gauges required to obtain — 24° = 27° - 3° 

10' -=9' + r 
and 18* = 18* 

Therefore the requi 3d angle is obtained by the combination of: 
(27° -3°) + (9 + 1') + 18* 




FIG. 3 BUILDING ANGLES USING ANGLE GAUGES 

b) Using Set B 

Gauges required to obtain — 24° = 30° - 5° - 1° 

10' -30' -20' 
and 18*- 12' + 6' 

Hence the required angle is obtained by the combination: 

( 30° ~ 5° ~ 1° ) + ( 30' - 20' ) + ( 12* + 6* ) 

Example 2: 

To build an angle : 29° 50' 9* 

a) Using Set A 

The fraction of a degree exceeds 40', therefore the angle may be written as: 

30°-. 10+9' 



IS: 6231 -1971 

Gauges required to build up the required angle in this case are: 

30° - 27° + 3° 
10'= 9+1' 
and ^ fa* = 6* ( The nearest gauge that can be used with an error of +3* ) . 

Therefore ihe angle - ( 27° + 3° ) - ( 9' + 1 ' > + 6* 
with an error of +3 sec. 

b) Using Set B 

29° = 30°- 1° 
50' «= 30' + 20' 
and 9* = 6* ( The nearest gauge with an error of +3* ). 

Therefore, the angle = ( 30° - 1° ) + ( 30' + 20 r ) + 6' 

with an error of +3*. * 

Not* — Any angle beyond 81° in the case of Set A and 90° in the case of Set B, can be obtained by suitably using 
the precision square block provided along with each set. 

A»2. Examples of Building Angles Using Angle Gauges Along with Precision Square Block 

ABC D is the precision square block. ABEF, the angle gauge combination to give an angle x, is 
wrung on to the square block ABC D. 

Referring to figure, if we draw normals 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5 to faces AB,BC, CD, DA and FE y it is seen that 
proceeding in a clock-wise direction the angles between normals 5 and 1 is x, between 5 and 2 it is 
( 90 + x ), between 5 and 3, it is ( 1 80 + x ) and between 5 and 4 the angle being ( 270 + x ). Since 
it is possible to build angle x in increments of 6 sec, it is clear that any angle from to 360° in steps of 
6 sec. can be built up using the angle gauges and the precision square block. 




FIG. 4 USE OF PRECISION SQUARE BLOCK 



Example 1: 



Angle required 121* 15' 27' 

The angle can be written as: 

90° + 3ri827' 



IS: 6231 -1971 

Using angle gauges the angle 31° 15' 27* is built. This combination is then wrung on to the 
square block and the required angle 121° 15' 27" is obtained. 

Referring to figure 4 the angle x in this case will be 31° 15' 27* and hence the angle between 
normals 5 and 2 in clockwise direction will give the required angle 121° 15' 27". 

Example 2: 

Angle required 306° 18' 42* 

This angle can be written as: 

270° + 36* « 8' 42* 

The angle 36° 18' 42" is built up using the angle gauges and the same in combination with the 
square block will give the required angle. 

Referring to figure 4, the angle x in this case will be 36° 18' 42" and the angle between fie 
normals 5 and 4 in clockwise direction will give the required angle 306° 18' 42".
